title: 🎮️ Dashboard command registry
description: 🎛️ Everything the dashboard can start is a registry command. Commands are discovered from Nx targets, the playground catalog, the repo domain and from the declarations this schema describes: `metadata.semio.dashboard` of a `📋️project.json` (`#/$defs/ProjectDeclaration`), `targets.<name>.metadata.semio.dashboard` (`#/$defs/TargetDeclaration`) and the `🎮️commands.json` of an open ticket (`#/$defs/TicketCommands`, the document this schema validates at its root). `#/$defs/ProjectManifest` validates the dashboard parts of a whole `📋️project.json`. The resolved outputs (`CommandId`, `RegistryEntry`, `TaskLabel`, `Ready`, `Launch`) are what `semio commands --json` and the daemon exchange.

Slug.description: 🔑️ A declared identifier: lowercase words joined by `-`, `.` or `_`. It never contains `/`, `:`, `=` or whitespace, so it stays unambiguous inside a command id and a `key=value` pair.

Verb.description: 🗂️ The verb a command is filed under (`dev`, `test`, `build`, …). A verb outside the launcher's verb list is listed after the known ones.

EnvName.description: 🌱️ An environment variable name. The runner variables the dashboard owns are never declared.

Text.description: 🔤️ One process word or environment value. Tokens: `{workspace}` is the workspace root, `{port}` the resolved ready port, `{<parameter id>}` the chosen value of a parameter. A literal absolute path is never stored; write `{workspace}/…`.

RelativePath.description: 📁️ A workspace-relative directory, forward-slashed; empty for the workspace root.

EnvMap.description: 🌱️ Variables added to the process environment.

NxFlags.description: 🚩️ Words placed before `--` of the Nx invocation (`--skip-nx-cache`, `--excludeTaskDependencies`, …). Commands that do not run Nx ignore them.

Args.description: ➡️ Words placed after `--` of the Nx invocation, or appended to a tool's command.

AppliesTo.description: 🎯️ Where a global axis is offered: on every command with a listed verb (tools included: their `nxFlags` are ignored, and an axis with nothing else to say is not offered on them), and on playgrounds when `playground` is true. Without `appliesTo` the axis is offered on every command Nx runs.

ParameterValue.description: 🎚️ One value of a choice together with its effect.

id.description: 🔑️ The value as chosen and as substituted for `{<parameter id>}`.

Parameter.description: 🎛️ Something chosen at launch. A `choice` carries one effect per value, a `flag` one effect when switched on, a `text` states where the typed value goes. Effect semantics: `env` is added to the process environment, `nxFlags` go before `--`, `args` after `--`.

appliesTo.description: 🎯️ Global axes only (parameters of the workspace root project).

default.description: 🧷️ The value applied when nothing is chosen; absent: not applied unless chosen. A choice names one of its values, a flag states `true` or `false`.

required.description: ❗️ The command does not start without a value.

valueEnv.description: 🌱️ The typed text becomes this environment variable.

valueFlag.description: 🚩️ The typed text follows this flag after `--`: two words, or one word when the flag ends with `=`.

valuePositional.description: ➡️ The typed text is one word after `--`.

ReadyDeclaration.description: 🟢️ The task is ready when its output shows `http://(127.0.0.1|localhost|0.0.0.0):<port>`; the ready URL is that match plus `path`. With `portEnv` and `port` the port is also exported under that variable; without `port`, `portEnv` names the parameter or environment value that carries it.

printed.description: 🖨️ The ready address is the whole printed address (up to whitespace) instead of the match plus `path`; it leaves no room for `path`.

AgentClientId.description: 🤖️ An agent or editor client whose MCP configuration file `bun ./📜️script.ts agents write` derives: `.mcp.json`, `.vscode/mcp.json`, `.cursor/mcp.json`, `.codex/config.toml`.

McpExposure.description: 🔌️ The tool is an MCP stdio server the listed clients start. `server` is its name in the client files; `command` of the tool is the process and each client states the value of every `text` parameter that is positional or a flag (a parameter without a value falls back to its `default`).

Tool.description: 🧰️ A command that is not an Nx target: `command` is the argument list, started in `cwd`.

verb.description: 🗂️ Default: the leading word of `id` when it is a known verb, else `task`.

continuous.description: ♾️ The tool keeps running until it is stopped.

Member.description: 🧩️ A reference to another command, plain or with the parameter values and environment it is pinned to. `env` is how a compound or a requirement states a relationship between commands (the hub address a shell joins); values may use `{workspace}`.

Requires.description: 🔗️ Services started (or reused) and awaited before the command starts.

Compound.description: 🧭️ Several commands started in order, each after the previous member is ready when that member declares `ready`.

verb.description: 🗂️ Default: the leading word of `id` when it is a known verb, else the verb of the first member.

stop.description: 🛑️ `together` stops all members when one stops; default `independent`.

Group.description: 👥️ One or more targets over a named project set (`nx run-many`).

targets.description: 🎯️ The targets `nx run-many` runs over the projects.

projects.description: 📋️ Project names or Nx project patterns: `*` matches any run of characters, a leading `!` excludes.

TargetDeclaration.description: 🎯️ `targets.<name>.metadata.semio.dashboard`: what the dashboard knows about one Nx target beyond Nx itself.

verb.description: 🗂️ Default: the leading word of the target name when it is a known verb, else `task`.

parameters.description: 🎛️ Target-owned parameters; one with the id of a global axis replaces that axis on this target.

ProjectDeclaration.description: 📋️ `metadata.semio.dashboard` of a project: tools, compounds and groups it owns. `parameters` are the global axes and belong to the workspace root project only.

TicketCommands.description: 🎫️ `<ticket folder>/🎮️commands.json`: the tools and compounds of one ticket, offered while the ticket is open.

ProjectManifest.description: 📋️ The dashboard parts of a whole `📋️project.json`; every other member is Nx's.

CommandId.description: 🪪️ The identity of a command. Chosen parameters follow an id as `key=value` pairs.

oneOf.description: 🛝️ A playground variant of the generated catalog.
🦑️ A repo-domain action answered in process.

TaskLabel.description: 🏷️ What a running task is called. Tab text and window title are pure functions of it: `verb subject [qualifier]`.

owner.description: 🧭️ The taxonomy path of the owner, outermost first.

qualifier.description: 🔖️ What tells this task from its siblings (target, configuration, renderer); may be empty.

members.description: 🧩️ The number of processes of a compound; 0 for a single process.

Ready.description: 🟢️ The resolved readiness of a process: ready when its output shows `http://(127.0.0.1|localhost|0.0.0.0):<port>`; the ready URL is that match plus `path`.

printed.description: 🖨️ The ready address is the whole printed address, not the match plus `path`.

ParameterInfo.description: 🎛️ One parameter a command accepts, as listed.

RegistryEntry.description: 📇️ One command as `semio commands --json` lists it.

listed.description: 👁️ Whether the command belongs to the default searchable set; the commands of a closed ticket do not.

mutating.description: ⚠️ Whether running the command changes repository state and deserves a confirmation.

mcp.description: 🔌️ Present when the command is an MCP stdio server the agent clients start.

source.description: 📄️ The workspace-relative file that declares the command; empty for commands built into the dashboard.

LaunchProcess.description: ▶️ One process of a resolved launch.

cwd.description: 📁️ Workspace-relative working directory, forward-slashed; empty for the workspace root.

Launch.description: 🚀️ `(id, chosen parameters, extra arguments)` resolved: the processes in start order, what must be ready first and how the group stops.

requires.description: 🔗️ Services started (or reused) and awaited before the first process starts.

group.description: 🧭️ The compound the processes belong to; absent for a single process.
